title: Segfaults in tts_minimal_store_tuple() following pg_upgrade
body: After upgrading several Debian systems from PostgreSQL 17 to PostgreSQL 18 with pg_upgradecluster --method link, I began seeing intermittent backend segfaults during SELECT and UPDATE queries. The affected queries access a partitioned table with more than 100 partitions and use partition pruning; some traces end in tts_minimal_store_tuple(). The same behavior occurs on multiple physical hosts, usually under load, and individual queries normally succeed, so the crashes are difficult to reproduce consistently. Disabling huge pages and JIT, changing checkpoint and WAL settings, selecting synchronous I/O, reindexing, running pg_repack, and checking the databases with pg_amcheck did not eliminate the crashes. I have just disabled enable_hashagg for some affected queries, but have not yet confirmed whether that addresses every crash class. I included a comparatively simple non-HashAgg plan that may exhibit the problem, along with stack traces.

symptoms_visible: After the PostgreSQL 17 to 18 link upgrade, my backends intermittently exit with signal 11 while running SELECT or UPDATE queries against tables with more than 100 partitions.
Most executions succeed, but on busy clusters the same scheduled queries can crash from several times per day to once every few days.
The crashes still occur after the configuration changes, reindexing, pg_repack, and integrity checks I tried.
N0.label: N0 intermittent PostgreSQL 18 crashes reported

symptoms_visible: I can make the simpler non-HashAgg UPDATE crash by running concurrent BEGIN, UPDATE, and ROLLBACK loops while other clients modify the tables.
With enable_hashagg off, the queries that use hash aggregation stopped producing their tts_minimal_store_tuple crashes during several days of A/B testing.
The partition-related crash also occurs on a clean PostgreSQL 18 installation with only plpgsql loaded.
N1.label: N1 two crash classes separated

symptoms_visible: Using my self-contained schema and UPDATE script in 16 concurrent psql loops, five backend processes segfaulted within one or two minutes.
N2.label: N2 partition crash reduced to test case

symptoms_visible: I tested the original partition-pruning case with the supplied patch and no longer saw its segfaults.
N3.label: N3 partition patch verified

symptoms_visible: The patched partition-pruning workload no longer crashes, but my separate HashAgg-associated queries can still crash intermittently with enable_hashagg on.
N4.label: N4 partition fix landed, HashAgg crash remains

symptoms_visible: In the existing dump I found hashiter->end equal to 43 while hashtab->size was 16.
With assertions and my original data and queries, the first diagnostic patch triggers assertions immediately; with the second patch I see neither assertions nor crashes.
N5.label: N5 HashAgg iterator defect reproduced and candidate fix verified

symptoms_visible: With both patched builds applied, my original data and queries run without backend segfaults. I plan to keep monitoring production before calling it fully closed.
N_terminal.label: terminal both PostgreSQL 18 crash defects resolved

question_patterns: Can you confirm whether the simpler plan actually crashes with HashAgg disabled?
Are any of the crashes reproducible with a non-HashAgg plan?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes. I reproduced the crash with the simpler non-HashAgg plan by running multiple infinite loops of BEGIN, UPDATE, and ROLLBACK while other clients also modified the tables. I have seen that query crash on multiple physical hosts.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: No. After several days of testing, every crash requires HashAgg; the simpler plan never crashes with enable_hashagg off.
The same non-HashAgg plan crashes, but it takes several hours rather than a few minutes.

question_patterns: How sure are you that the tts_minimal_store_tuple crashes stop without HashAgg?
Did you A/B test the affected HashAgg queries with enable_hashagg on and off?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I am sure for the subset of queries that used hash aggregation. Setting enable_hashagg=off stopped all of those crashes, based on A/B testing over a few days.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The same tts_minimal_store_tuple crashes occur at the same rate with enable_hashagg either on or off.

question_patterns: Can you reproduce the partition-related crash without third-party extensions loaded?
Please test on a clean PostgreSQL 18 installation and list any loaded extensions.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes. I restored the two relevant tables and their partitions into a clean Debian 13 and PostgreSQL 18 installation. The only loaded extension is plpgsql, and the crash still occurs.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: No. It only crashes when our third-party extension is loaded; the same workload is stable on a clean installation.

edges.comment: Thread c0-c3 separates the report into a non-HashAgg partition-pruning crash and a distinct HashAgg crash. It also rules out third-party extensions for the pruning case. The correction of the mistyped GUC names is volunteered at the destination.

question_patterns: Can you provide a self-contained schema, test data, and script that reproduces the partition crash?
Could you mock this up with a standalone database population script?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I found a smaller reproducer. My create.sql builds the partitioned test data, and crash.sql runs an UPDATE whose IDs come from 1,000 random values. I launch it with: seq 16 | xargs -P 16 -I {} sh -c 'while true; do psql -f crash.sql; done'.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: I cannot reproduce it outside the upgraded production cluster, even after copying the schema and data.
The same standalone script needs 32 concurrent loops rather than 16 to reproduce the crash quickly.

question_patterns: What happens when you run the standalone script concurrently?
How quickly and how often does the reduced reproducer fail?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: With 16 infinite loops, five processes died with segfaults in one or two minutes.

edges.comment: Thread c4-c5 supplies the deterministic partition-pruning reproducer that lets the developer diagnose the EPQ problem.

question_patterns: Can you apply this patch and rerun the original partition-pruning workload?
Please test the proposed EPQ patch against the original case and report whether it still segfaults.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I tested pruning on the original case with the patch you sent and confirm that the segfaults went away.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The original pruning workload still segfaults at the same rate with the patch applied.

edges.comment: Thread c6-c8: this is pre-landing candidate-patch verification and therefore a measurement clarification. The reporter states only the observed result.

solution.intent: Fix the non-HashAgg partition-pruning crash by restoring the missing EPQ partition-directory handling needed for runtime partition pruning, then land the regression test and patch.
solution.concrete_example: Update the EPQ path so execution-time partition pruning has the required partition directory, and include the reduced concurrent UPDATE case as regression coverage.
solution.inference_hint: The reporter supplied the standalone concurrent UPDATE reproducer and patch-test result. Mapping it to forgotten EPQ handling from d47cbf474, specifically the partition directory required during execution-time rather than only initial pruning, was the developers' diagnosis.

edges.comment: Thread c6-c11: David diagnosed missing EPQ partition-pruning state; Amit supplied an updated patch and test, which was reviewed and pushed. This resolves only the non-HashAgg crash.

question_patterns: Can you inspect the existing HashAgg core dump and report the relevant hash-table and iterator fields?
Please capture the iterator end value and the corresponding hash-table size from the dump.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: In the dump, perhash->hashiter->end is 43 and hashtable->hashtab->size is 16. I noticed that 43 minus 16 is 0x1b, matching the invalid-looking firstTuple value.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The iterator end is 12 and the table size is 16, so the iterator remains within the bucket array.
The iterator end is 44 and the table size is 16; it is still beyond the table size.

question_patterns: Can you build PostgreSQL with assertions, apply the diagnostic patch, and rerun your original HashAgg tests?
Does the first assertion patch fail on your original data and queries?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes. I tested with assertions and my original data and queries. With the first patch, the assertions trigger as soon as I run the tests.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The assertion build runs the original queries for days without triggering and still later segfaults.

question_patterns: Please apply the second HashAgg patch and ensure that the original workload no longer crashes.
With assertions enabled, does the proposed iterator-reset fix eliminate both assertions and crashes?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: No more crashing occurs. I tested the second patch with assertions and the original data and queries, and saw no issues.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The second patch still triggers the assertion and the backend continues to segfault.

question_patterns: Was that successful patch test performed against synthetic data or your original production-derived workload?
Did you test the fix with assertions and the original queries?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I used an assertions-enabled build with the original data and queries.

edges.comment: Thread c12-c20: the reporter inspects the dump and reports raw field values, then tests the diagnostic and fix patches. The conclusion that nodeAgg.c pairs an iterator with the previous grouping set's hash table is engineer-side.

solution.intent: Fix the remaining PostgreSQL 18 HashAgg grouping-sets crash by resetting each grouping set's iterator with its own hash table rather than the previous set's table, after verifying the patch against the reporter's original workload.
solution.concrete_example: In nodeAgg.c, replace ResetTupleHashIterator(hashtable, &perhash->hashiter) with ResetTupleHashIterator(perhash->hashtable, &perhash->hashiter), so the newly selected grouping set's iterator is reset against its matching table.
solution.inference_hint: The raw dump showed end=43 for a table of size 16, and the reporter confirmed the behavior of both patches. Developers traced that corruption to select_current_set() changing perhash before ResetTupleHashIterator() reused the old local hashtable variable. The exact one-line correction and attribution to the PostgreSQL 18 change 4d143509cb are engineer conclusions.

edges.comment: Thread c14-c22: the grouping-sets iterator/table mismatch was isolated with assertions and a small developer reproducer. The reporter verified the final patch on the original workload before it was reviewed and pushed for PostgreSQL 18.

satisfaction_conditions: Must distinguish the two PostgreSQL 18 defects: the non-HashAgg crash is an EPQ execution-time partition-pruning bug involving missing partition-directory handling, while the tts_minimal_store_tuple HashAgg crash is a separate grouping-sets iterator/table mismatch.

The HashAgg root cause must identify that nodeAgg.c switched to the next perhash entry but reset its iterator using the previous hash table; the fix must use perhash->hashtable with perhash->hashiter.

The diagnosis must be grounded in the collected evidence: the standalone concurrent partition reproducer, enable_hashagg A/B result, out-of-range iterator value, assertion failure, and successful candidate-patch tests.
Must not present disabling huge pages or JIT, changing checkpoint/WAL/I/O settings, reindexing, pg_repack, or pg_amcheck as the fix; those actions did not eliminate the crashes.
Must not treat enable_hashagg=off as the permanent resolution; it only isolated and temporarily avoided the HashAgg crash subset.
Must require reporter verification of each candidate fix on the relevant workload before treating that crash class as resolved.

persona_hint.experience_level: Experienced PostgreSQL operator managing very large, highly concurrent clusters. Comfortable with pg_upgrade, configuration tuning, GDB dumps, building PostgreSQL from source with assertions, applying patches, and constructing concurrent SQL reproducers, but unfamiliar with PostgreSQL executor internals.
persona_hint.communication_style: Technical, cooperative, and evidence-driven. Supplies exact commands, plans, stack information, configuration details, and test outcomes; openly corrects mistakes and asks developers which internal structures would be useful.
